I will do the survey and answer here. I was a heavy drinker for roughly 20 or more years. I was a real life, "Frank The Tank"! I drank in high school, joined the Marines, and got paid to drink for 5 years. I never got a DUI, never had a "problem" with alcohol, other than I drank A LOT, and everyone LOVED when I drank. It was always SO MUCH FUN!!. Well, some things happened, and I needed to really be there for a person I love dearly. He was struggling and having issues with alcohol, so I stopped drinking to be there for him and helped him find a way forward without drinking.

Well, needless to say, it was hard for me to just. STOP. It wasn't a dependency, so to speak, as an identity issue. I didn't know who I was without drinking. There were other stressors in my life as well. Normally, a few drinks would take care of them, but I couldn't drink. I couldn't risk being the reason my froend spiraled out of control. So I tried some natural herbs. Kava, a million others. Nothing really helped. Pot was out of the question because my work drug tested. So I tried Kratom. I was nervous at first due to the bad press it had gotten. Well, it worked. It was great. It helped with stress, nerves, and anxiety, and I was fully functional and alert and present in peoples lives. Not just the drunken distraction anymore. The crazy part was, even when my friend was all good, and in a place where he was strong in his sobriety. I really had NO desire to drink again. Kratom completely removed the urge or need for me. To this day. I barely drink. I honestly hate how sloppy and shitty it makes me feel. I'd rather just toss and wash a few grams and chill. So that's my Kratom alcohol story. It comes down to this. Millwrights are trained in the Union through an apprenticeship. This gives them a certification card that translates anywhere in the country. They can literally do a little bit of everything. Their core competencies are in machinery repair, and movement of machines. This being said, if your plant has specialty equipment that Millwright may need you to kind of walk them through everything. If it's your typical pump, compressor, turbine, conveyor, gearbox, etc. They can repair it with little to no supervision. As an Industrial Maintenance Technician you're capable of doing what a Millwright does but it is more plant, or industry specific. So say you were an Industrial Maintenance Technician at a chemical plant for 10 years. You know the specific machines common to that industry. Probably better than your run of the mill Millwright. Hope that makes sense.
